newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Nobel peace prize winner says both happy and sad.
newsitem.headline: Nobel peace prize winner says both happy and sad.

text.p: Nobel Peace Prize winner Jose Ramos-Horta, a spokesman for the East Timor resistance movement, said on Friday that he was happy but also sad at the award because his jailed leader Xanana Gusmao should have won.
"I receive the news with pleasure and with sadness," Ramos-Horta, who was honoured along with East Timor Bishop Carlos Belo, said in a radio interview.
Ramos-Horta, who is in Sydney, Australia, said that he had pressed "my friends in Scandanavia that...they should also propose Xanana (Gusmao)."
Gusmao has been in prison in Jakarta, Indonesia, since 1992 when he was captured by Indonesian security forces and sentenced to 20 years in jail.

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975, just after Portugal pulled out, and annexed the territory a year later. The annexation has never been recognised by the United Nations.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee said that Ramos-Horta and Belo had been awarded the prize for "their work toward a just and peaceful solution to the conflict in East Timor."
